title: Bensalem
name: Bensalem
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for I-95 and turnpike-corridor industrial, casino and outlet-adjacent retail, and garden apartments in Bensalem, Pennsylvania.

sections.html: Bensalem Township sits at the point where I-95 meets the Pennsylvania Turnpike's Delaware Valley extension, an interchange dense enough that logistics users have followed it for decades alongside Parx Casino and Racing and the retail corridor around Philadelphia Mills. An investor here is typically choosing among industrial and flex product built for that highway access, retail leased along Street Road and Route 1, or garden-style multifamily serving the township's working population. Each of these asset types answers to a different tenant base, so the diligence checklist looks different depending on which one an investor is naming.

sections.heading: Highway Access Is the Product Being Sold
sections.html: Industrial and flex buildings in Bensalem compete on distance to the I-95 and turnpike interchange more than on raw square footage, and a building close to that access point can retrofit clear height and loading at a lower cost per square foot than an equivalent building farther out toward the older Woodhaven Road industrial parks. Confirming actual truck routing and trailer parking capacity matters more here than a simple drive-time estimate on a map, since a route that looks short in miles can run long once local turning restrictions and signal timing are factored in.

sections.heading: Retail Leaning on Parx and Philadelphia Mills Traffic
sections.html: Strip retail and pad sites along Street Road draw meaningful visitor volume from Parx Casino and Philadelphia Mills, but that traffic supports the surrounding retail unevenly depending on lease structure. A standalone pad with a fixed-rent, credit tenant tends to hold up better through a casino or mall slowdown than in-line space leased on percentage rent tied to the anchor's own performance. An investor should also confirm whether a given lease carries a co-tenancy clause that could reduce rent if the mall's own occupancy drops below a set threshold, since that clause changes the practical income floor on the property.

sections.heading: Multifamily Demand Tracks the Airport and Warehouse Workforce
sections.html: Garden apartment complexes here largely serve workers tied to nearby airport and logistics employment rather than a downtown professional tenant base, and rent growth tends to be modest but occupancy steady. Many of these complexes date to the 1970s and 1980s, so a real capital-improvement history should factor into the purchase price alongside the current rent roll, not in place of it. Roof age, HVAC replacement schedules, and parking-lot condition tend to be the items that surface as unexpected costs after closing when they were not documented before the identification deadline.

sections.heading: Identification, Diligence, and Bensalem's Own Permitting Process
sections.html:
Bensalem runs its own zoning, building permits, and Uniform Construction Code inspections through its own township process, separate from Philadelphia's use-and-occupancy certificate system a few miles south, and the realty transfer tax here follows the standard state-plus-local combination rather than Philadelphia's higher combined city rate. A Bensalem diligence file typically includes:

  • Traffic count and interchange access study for industrial or retail parcels
  • Tenant estoppels for casino- or mall-adjacent retail leases
  • Phase I environmental review for older industrial buildings
  • Rent roll and capital-improvement history for garden multifamily
  • Zoning confirmation with Bensalem Township for any proposed change of use

sections.heading: What Works for Bensalem Exchangers
sections.html: Investors who treat highway access as the actual asset being purchased, underwrite casino- and mall-adjacent retail on lease terms rather than location alone, and confirm capital-improvement history before relying on an older multifamily rent roll tend to close cleaner deals in this submarket than those chasing traffic counts alone. The 45-day identification window moves the same regardless of asset type, which is why getting the diligence checklist right for the specific property matters more than a generic Bensalem overview. An investor working from an office building or a downtown retail strip elsewhere in the metro should expect Bensalem's underwriting conversation to focus on interchange distance and tenant traffic dependency in a way those other submarkets simply do not require to the same degree.

faqs.q: How does Bensalem's permitting process differ from Philadelphia's?
faqs.a: Bensalem Township runs its own zoning and building-permit process with third-party Uniform Construction Code inspections, distinct from Philadelphia's use-and-occupancy certificate system. Confirm current township requirements directly rather than assuming city rules carry over.

faqs.q: Is retail near Parx Casino a stable 1031 replacement property?
faqs.a: It can be, but the answer depends on the lease's rent structure. A fixed-rent, credit tenant on a standalone pad generally carries less income variability than in-line space leased on percentage rent tied to casino attendance.

faqs.q: What financing questions come up with older Bensalem industrial near I-95?
faqs.a: Lenders typically want a realistic clear-height and loading-dock retrofit estimate before underwriting a rent increase, since older buildings near the interchange were not all built to modern logistics specifications. Getting that estimate early avoids financing delays close to the identification deadline.

faqs.q: How many replacement properties should I identify if I'm comparing industrial, retail, and multifamily in Bensalem?
faqs.a: If the comparable pool across those asset types is thin in a given quarter, the 200% rule often gives more flexibility than the three-property rule, since it allows identifying more candidates as long as their combined value stays within the cap.

faqs.q: What capital items should I expect to find on an older Bensalem garden apartment complex?
faqs.a: Roof age, HVAC replacement schedule, and parking-lot condition are the most common items that surface as unbudgeted costs on complexes built in the 1970s and 1980s, so requesting maintenance records before identification is worth the effort.

faqs.q: Can this service tell me for certain whether my Bensalem property qualifies for 1031 treatment?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates identification, timeline management, and communication among the investor's advisors. A qualifying determination comes from the investor's own CPA, tax attorney, and qualified intermediary.
